prediction.text: Bank of America is asset-sensitive, so a sudden 100 basis point drop in rates would reduce its net interest income. In the "Interest Rate Risk Management for the Banking Book" section of its 10-K, it shows the estimated 12-month impact of instantaneous shifts in the yield curve. In recent filings, a 100 bp parallel decline reduced NII by a couple of billion dollars, which is only a few percent of its roughly $55-57 billion in annual NII. The cause is that floating-rate loans and cash reprice down faster than deposit costs can fall. Hedges such as receive-fixed swaps and the securities portfolio offset part of the decline. I don't remember the exact figure for the latest period, and it changes from filing to filing, so check the sensitivity table in the most recent 10-K or 10-Q for the precise number.
